restatements.text: Allows a person 21 or older who may lawfully possess a handgun to carry it concealed without a permit.
Requires sheriffs to continue issuing concealed carry permits on request to qualified applicants for use in other states.

analysis.answer: Current law requires individuals to complete an eight-hour safety course and obtain a permit from the county sheriff to carry a concealed handgun. This clause removes these requirements for in-state carry.
This clause preserves the existing permit issuance process on a voluntary basis for individuals who want a permit for out-of-state reciprocity.

Direct costs may include a loss of permit fee revenue for sheriffs, though fees are not explicitly mentioned in the text. There is an opportunity cost for firearm instructors, who will lose students who previously took the mandatory safety course.
Individuals 21 or older who wish to carry a concealed handgun benefit by avoiding the time and expense of a class and permit. Firearm safety instructors bear the cost of reduced demand.
More people will likely carry concealed handguns because the barriers of mandatory training and permitting are removed. Demand for eight-hour safety courses will drop significantly.

The measure addresses the entry barrier of mandatory training and permitting for carrying a concealed handgun. By removing the mandate, it also removes a mechanism (the safety course) that addresses the potential spillover risks of untrained individuals carrying concealed weapons.
Individuals gain the discretion to carry concealed handguns without state permission. Sheriffs lose the power to restrict in-state concealed carry to those who have completed safety training.

It is empirically disputed whether permitless carry laws increase crime or firearm accidents. Some researchers find that removing permit and training requirements increases firearm-related violence, while others find no significant effect or argue it deters crime.
Removing the permit requirement likely reduces the administrative workload and enforcement burden on county sheriffs regarding in-state concealed carry.
